title: Train a Cellpose model
description: Prepare image/mask pairs, fine-tune a segmentation model in the Cellpose Workbench and apply the saved checkpoint.
objectives: Load matching images and object-label masks.
Choose the starting model, training settings and output folder.
Run training, find the checkpoint and try it on separate images.
prerequisite: Download and extract the linked six-pair example, or prepare your own images and matching integer-label masks. Inspect and correct the masks in Make Masks before training.

scenes.narration: From Home, open Tools, then Make Masks. Open Cellpose Workbench from its toolbar and choose the Train tab. You will train from images and their object-label masks, then use the saved model in Apply.

Extract the linked example and set Source to its training folder. The folder contains six images and a masks subfolder. Leave mask source empty to use that subfolder, or choose a separate folder containing your masks.

Each image needs one matching mask with the same height and width. Mask values identify objects: zero is background and each object has its own positive integer. Inspect the boundaries in Make Masks and correct labels before using them for training.

For this grayscale example, leave the channel selection empty. For a multichannel image, select up to three zero-based channel indices, such as zero and two for the first and third channels. Set channel axis if automatic detection cannot identify the channel dimension.

Choose a base model. The default cpsam starts from Cellpose-SAM; a checkpoint path continues training an existing model. Enter a model name and choose Save path for the output, or leave it empty to save inside the project.

Set the number of epochs and the batch size. For a quick first run, use two epochs and batch size one. More epochs give the model more training updates, and larger batches use more memory. Learning rate controls the update size; begin with the displayed default.

Keep normalization on with the first and ninety-ninth percentiles as a starting point. These control the intensity range used for each channel. Scale range controls variation in image size during training. Minimum training masks excludes images with too few labelled objects.

To monitor validation loss, choose a separate validation image folder and its matching masks. Keep these fields separate from the training inputs. Leave the validation folders empty when you do not have a separate set.

Review the input folders, model name and output location, then press Run. Follow training progress in the console. When the run finishes, the console gives the checkpoint path to use for segmentation.

With an explicit Save path, look inside its models subfolder. With the default location, the checkpoint is inside the source folder under models, cellpose_model, models. Keep the checkpoint with your training settings.

Open Apply and choose a separate image folder. Check that Custom model points to the checkpoint you want, then inspect a preview before running the whole folder. Apply writes masks beside those images in a masks subfolder. Use separate labelled fields to evaluate the results.
